warmup.text: This is the last week of How I Became a Ghost. In Chapter 28, the wolf comes back, and Naomi has to choose in a moment. This week you also set the novel beside real history. Start noticing what only a story can tell you.

words.text: This week's words are the ones a historian uses with care: claim, evidence, reasoning, treaty, removal, nation. Then formal style, the way an essay talks. In the game, peel the husks off a long word to find the base word inside.

reading.text: Read Chapter 28 in your book. Watch the panther and the wolf, and listen to what Naomi says when Leader asks her why. Then study the Read Like a Writer sentence, and finish with the Virtue Watch.

assignment.text: Three questions about Chapter 28. Then plan your source comparison. You need a claim, one detail from the novel, one line from a real source, and your reasoning. Today you only plan.

hook.q: The person who hurt you is in danger. Only you can help. Do you?

options.t: Yes. It is the right thing.
options.reply: That is hard to do. In Chapter 28, someone is asked why she did it. She answers:

options.t: No. Not after what they did.
options.reply: That is an honest answer, and many people would feel the same. In Chapter 28, someone chooses differently. When she is asked why, she says:
It is a hard question. In Chapter 28, someone has only a moment to decide. Afterward she says:

reveal.line: It was the right thing to do. It is the Choctaw way.
reveal.then: As you read Chapter 28, find out who says this, and whom she helps.

glossary.meaning: something written or made at the time, by someone who was there
something written later, by someone who studied the event

miss.declaration: The ending is -ation. Say the last part: it sounds like ay-shun.
miss.displacement: The ending is -ment, added to a whole word.
miss.government: govern + ment. Do not lose the n before -ment.
miss.negotiation: The ending is -ation. Say the last part: it sounds like ay-shun.
miss.relocation: The ending is -ation. Say the last part: it sounds like ay-shun.
miss.settlement: The ending is -ment, added to a whole word.
miss.liberty: The ending is -ty, as in safety and loyalty.

game.title: Ears of Corn
game.sub: This week's word game · 3 words today
game.look: Each long word is an ear of corn, like the corn the families cook in Chapter 29. The parts added to the front or the end are the husks. Tap each husk to peel it away. The base word is the ear inside.

do: Read the long word.
Find the part that can stand alone as a word. Leave it.
Tap each part added to the front or the end.
Tap Next word.
how.why: Long words in history writing are short words with parts added. Find the base and you can read and spell the rest.

game.doneLine: Come back tomorrow for three more words.

ears.why: mis- means badly, and -ment makes a noun.
un- means not, and -ness makes a noun.
ears.means: the state of not being fair.

art.title: Black American Wolf
art.alt: A hand-colored print of a black wolf running across open grassland with its mouth open.
art.look: This print comes from The Viviparous Quadrupeds of North America, a book of animal pictures by John James Audubon and his sons, printed in 1845. John Woodhouse Audubon, his son, drew this wolf. Viviparous quadrupeds means four-legged animals that give birth to live young. In Chapter 28, the wolf returns.

virtue.name: courage
virtue.title: Courage or not?
virtue.intro: You just read Chapter 28. Read each moment. Tap Courage or Not courage.

items.t: Joseph, as the panther, leaps between the wolf and Leader.
items.why: He risks himself to save a man who tried to kill him.

items.t: Naomi says, “We cannot let this happen,” about the man who vowed she would die.
items.why: Doing right by an enemy is one of the hardest kinds of courage.

items.t: Leader kicks the dead wolf so it lands at Naomi's feet.
items.why: The danger is already over. Showing off your strength takes no courage.

items.t: Roundman aims his shotgun at Naomi and Joseph and shouts.
items.why: Pointing a weapon at two children who just saved a life is not brave.
